paper.title_en: Proton Structure and QCD under the LHC Neutrino Microscope
paper.abstract_en: The LHC produces an abundant flux of high-energy neutrinos and muons in the far-forward rapidity region. The neutrinos reach energies in the TeV range, which makes them the highest-energy neutrinos ever produced in a lab environment.In this thesis, scientific opportunities are explored to exploit the neutrino and muon flux to investigate the substructure of the proton. The impact of neutrino deep-inelastic scattering (DIS) measurements at the ongoing FASERν experiment and the planned detectors at the proposed Forward Physics Facility (FPF) on global Parton Distribution Function (PDF) extractions is assessed.A detailed phenomenological analysis of the DIS process is performed with state-of-the-art Monte Carlo simulation at next-to leading order in QCD expansion.This Monte Carlo simulation pipeline is then used to produce theory prediction that are required for a first machine-learning based extraction of the muon neutrino flux from FASER 2024 data. Fits of the neutrino flux allow to discriminate between different models of forward hadron production, constrain rare beyond the Standard Model decays to neutrinos and potentially provide evidence for the presence or absence of an intrinsic charm component of the proton.In the last part of the thesis, muon DIS is studied, which can probe the charm content of the proton directly, especially in the large-x region. This kinematic region is of special interest when searching for evidence for intrinsic charm. The analysis shows that the FASERν experiment could provide competitive constraints on intrinsic charm. Combining the FASERν emulsion detector with the electronic FASER detector it is also possible to construct a charm-asymmetry observable. A non-zero charm-asymmetrywould provide conclusive evidence for intrinsic charm
